claims.statement: Low-level instructions change the planning burden; grounding-only evaluations do not test full task execution.
GUIOdyssey uses model-generated annotations over human demonstrations; the methods section separately explains OpenCUA.

Action counts, model calls and elapsed cost are distinct; retries and failure budgets affect efficiency interpretation.
Human reference trajectories reflect permitted tools and are not proven shortest paths over unrestricted computer operations.
Judge validation, raw-versus-corrected outcomes and evaluator versions are needed to interpret measurement changes.
Task success, helpful refusal, misuse, injection and unintended harm require separate outcome definitions.
Security findings are conditional on attacker control and should not be pooled across incompatible threat models.
Attack encounter, attempted diversion and completed harm are separate stages; lack of exposure is not demonstrated resistance.
DIBench commercial-app trials measure fixed-state candidate decisions rather than live end-to-end transactions.
Installed-app architectural threats and compromised visual fine-tuning data are distinct from runtime webpage injection.
Trajectory safety scores are fallible evaluator contracts, requiring utility and human-agreement reporting.
Recommendation: publish the complete evaluation contract, correction policy and failure denominators.
Recommendation: retain execution evidence and report capability, cost, shift and security outcomes separately.
Recommendation: distinguish code, data, weights and application access terms; publication or repository visibility is not a blanket grant.
